Let \(G=\mathbb F_2^4\). For a chosen set/multiset, let \(A\) be its support of parity vectors.

If \(A\) contains four distinct vectors summing to \(0\), then choosing one number from each gives a square product. Thus \(A\) must have all unordered pair sums of distinct elements distinct and nonzero. Hence
\[
\binom{|A|}{2}\le 15 \implies |A|\le 6.
\]
Also, in a valid multiset, no two distinct support vectors can both have multiplicity at least \(2\), and no vector can have multiplicity at least \(4\). Therefore the total number of chosen elements is at most
\[
|A|+2\le 6+2=8.
\]
So any subset of \(S\) of size \(9\) must contain the desired four numbers.

To see that \(8\) is not enough, take
\[
\{1,4,9,2,3,5,7,210\}.
\]
Their parity vectors are
\[
0000,0000,0000,1000,0100,0010,0001,1111.
\]
The support has no four distinct vectors summing to \(0\), and only \(0000\) is repeated, only three times. Hence this \(8\)-element subset has no four distinct numbers with square product.

Therefore the smallest such \(n\) is
\[
\boxed{9}.
\]
